How to give gifts
people actually remember
Listen all year long. When someone says "I'd love to try that" or "mine just broke," write it down. The best gifts come from small comments.
Give experiences, not just things. A cooking class, concert tickets, a day trip. Shared memories last much longer than objects.
Make it personal. A book with a handwritten note, a framed photo of a good day. Personal touches matter more than the price.
Wrap it with care. Nice paper, a ribbon, a short card. Presentation shows effort, and effort is what people really feel.
Before: I gave the same boring gifts every year. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I find ideas tied to real stories.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I gave the same boring gifts every year. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I find ideas tied to real stories.

slides.texte_overlay: Give for no reason. A small surprise on a random Tuesday often means more than a big present on a birthday. Small, unexpected and thoughtful wins every time.
Write something real in the card. Two honest sentences about what the person means to you. People keep those cards for years.
